The two developer-authored web acceptance specs (kotlin-flip-card.spec.ts, flip-rive-perf.spec.ts) pass 11/11 on both JS and Wasm branches in Chromium, and 11/11 on Firefox and WebKit for the JS branch. The quantitative §5 measurement protocol (frame p50/p95/p99, janky/dropped%, long tasks, memory, Rive first-effect latency) — which the plan's own evidence log says was NOT collected for web — is now collected for all 3 variants × 2 branches, ≥6 cycles each, with raw JSON + a combined CSV saved under Plans/Kotlin/artifacts/flip-rive/web/. The main open gap: memory-leak detection is inconclusive at this cycle count due to Chromium's memory-API quantization (a measurement-resolution limitation, not a product finding), and Firefox/WebKit have no quantitative numbers (API availability limitation). Neither indicates a product defect; both should be named explicitly rather than reported as clean data.

verdict: Two of the three requested variants were measured with real, reproducible evidence (gfxinfo, meminfo, CPU snapshot, and a precise APK-size delta); the third (native-flip-only) is blocked by a genuine, reachable-from-outside-the-process gap in the Android implementation and was correctly reported as not run rather than guessed. Within this run, flip+Rive shows no clear regression in janky-frame% or memory versus no-animation on this emulator, but the harness's own UI-automation overhead dominates the frame counts enough that this should be treated as 'no obvious red flag' rather than a validated performance sign-off -- a real on-device Macrobenchmark pass (with FrameTimingMetric isolating just the flip/rating gesture) is still needed before treating Android's flip+Rive cost as characterized. The APK size delta (+~26.8MB debug / ABI-unsplit, dominated by librive-android.so x4 ABIs) is solid, precise evidence and the single most actionable number from this pass.
